questions.text:
Let G be any connection, weighted, undirected graph:

I. G has a unique minimum spanning tree if no two edges of G have the same weight.
II. G has a unique minimum spanning tree if, for every cut of G, there is a unique minimum weight edge crossing the cut.

Which of the above two statements is/are TRUE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: with distinct weights, Kruskal never faces a tie, so the MST is unique [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- II: if every cut has a unique lightest crossing edge, the cut property forces that edge into every MST; this fixes the whole MST [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.

Answer: Both I and II

questions.text: There are n unsorted arrays: [latex]A_1,A_2,...,A_n[/latex]. Assume that n is odd. Each of [latex]A_1,A_2,...,A_n[/latex] contains n distinct elements. There are no common elements between any two arrays. The worst-case Asymptotic Notation of computing the median of the medians of [latex]A_1,A_2,...,A_n[/latex] is ________ .
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Median of each unsorted array of n elements (linear-time selection): [latex]O(n)[/latex] each, n arrays [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]O(n^2)[/latex].
- Median of those n medians: [latex]O(n)[/latex].

Total [latex]O(n^2)[/latex]. It cannot be less, because all [latex]n^2[/latex] elements must be looked at.

Answer: [latex]O(n^2)[/latex]

questions.text: Consider a sequence of 14 elements: A = [-5, -10, 6, 3, -1, -2, 13, 4, -9, -1, 4, 12, -3, 0]. The sequence sum [latex]S(i,j)=\sum_{k=i}^{j}A[k][/latex]. Determine the maximum of S(i,j), where [latex]0 \leq i \leq j \lt 14[/latex]. (Divide and conquer approach may be used). Answer:______
questions.solution:
Use Kadane's idea (running sum, restart when it goes negative):
[latex]-[/latex]5, [latex]-[/latex]10 are dropped. From 6: running sums 6, 9, 8, 6, 19, 23, 14, 13, 17, 29, 26, 26.

Maximum subarray = 6 + 3 [latex]-[/latex] 1 [latex]-[/latex] 2 + 13 + 4 [latex]-[/latex] 9 [latex]-[/latex] 1 + 4 + 12 = 29.

Answer: 29

questions.text: An array of 25 distinct elements is to be sorted using quicksort. Assume that the pivot element is chosen uniformly at random. The probability that the pivot element gets placed in the worst possible location in the first round of partitioning (rounded off to 2 decimal places) is _________.
questions.solution:
The worst position for the pivot is either end of the array, which happens when the pivot is the smallest or the largest element: 2 out of 25 choices.

[latex]P=\frac{2}{25}=0.08[/latex]

Answer: 0.08

questions.text: Of the following sorting algorithms, which has a running time that is least dependent on the initial ordering of the input?
questions.solution:
Merge sort always splits in half and merges: [latex]\Theta(n\log n)[/latex] for any input order. Insertion and quick sort change a lot with the input order.

Answer: Merge Sort
